etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English sovereyn, from Old French soverain (whence also modern French souverain), from Vulgar Latin *superānus (compare Italian sovrano, Spanish soberano) from Latin super (“above”). Spelling influenced by folk-etymology association with reign. Doublet of soprano, from the same Latin root via Italian. See also suzerain, foreign.

definitions.definition: (now rare, pharmacology) Extremely potent or effective (of a medicine, remedy etc.).
